title: A production caller that enqueues a graph, and a comparison that must actually compare
note: Two rows, one shape: a mechanism that existed and whose real question nothing asked. The scheduler could always express dependencies and the production path enqueued one job, so 'dependency graphs are exercised only in tests'. And the cross-environment comparison could always report IDENTICAL without comparing anything, because the verdict read one field instead of closing the arithmetic.

mutations.name: G1_dependencies_never_reach_the_scheduler
mutations.rationale: the ordering becomes the caller's loop again and the queue never sees a graph, which is the original defect

mutations.name: G2_a_dependent_step_requires_no_evidence
mutations.rationale: readiness becomes 'the parent job says SUCCEEDED' rather than 'the bytes it should have left behind resolve'

mutations.name: G3_a_step_runs_though_its_dependency_failed
mutations.find:
runnable = [sid for sid, (_t, _i, deps) in remaining.items()
                        if all(d in done for d in deps)]
mutations.rationale: work executes against a parent that produced nothing, and its BLOCKED outcome is reported as a run

mutations.name: G4_an_empty_graph_reports_success
mutations.rationale: a graph that ran nothing returns an empty result set, which every caller reads as 'no failures'

mutations.name: G5_a_dependency_on_a_missing_step_is_accepted
mutations.find:
unknown = [d for d in deps if d not in ids]
            if unknown:
mutations.replace:
unknown = [d for d in deps if d not in ids]
            if False:
mutations.rationale: a step that can never become ready is enqueued and silently dropped from the results

mutations.name: G6_duplicate_step_ids_are_accepted
mutations.rationale: two steps share a name and only one appears in the results, so a caller sees fewer runs than it asked for
